subject: English
subskill: Meaning of Word in Literary Prose
passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1919 play. Rivera and Shin are explaining to a visitor why their mill has replaced its hand-weavers with mechanized looms.

RIVERA: A single loom can do the work of four weavers, madam. The hand-weaver, I am sorry to say, was hopelessly slow. Some such change was bound to come.

SHIN: And ruinously costly.

RIVERA: It was not productive. It no longer answers the demands of modern industry. The old crafts cannot keep up with the pace that commerce requires today.
prompt: As used in the text, what does the word "answers" most nearly mean?
explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because as used in the text, "answers" most nearly means fulfills. In the passage, Rivera and Shin argue that mechanized looms are more efficient than hand-weavers. Rivera observes that the hand-weaver "no longer answers the demands of modern industry" — that is, hand-weavers are no longer able to meet or satisfy the rigorous requirements of modern commercial production.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. Although in some contexts "answers" can mean defends or justifies, it doesn't have that meaning here because Rivera's point is that hand-weavers can no longer meet the demands of modern industry, not that they have ceased to justify or defend those demands; nothing in the passage suggests that the demands themselves are under attack.
